title: Microfriction Skipper — Pocket Play (Draft)
body:
Purpose:
Make it trivial for SEs and sellers to turn a curious platform engineer or security reviewer into a pilot-ready champion in under 15 minutes. Focus is on removing friction in three lanes: procurement questions, platform integration, and SLA/canary comfort.

Audience:
- Sellers and SEs running pilot conversations with platform & security stakeholders
- Field ops and solutions engineers prepping a 30–90 day pilot

TL;DR (one-sentence):
Ship a 6-slide minimal deck + 3 canned scripts + pre-approved pilot artifacts bundle so the buyer can get a sandbox spun, a canary running, and a procurement checkbox ticked in one meeting.

What this deck is (and is not):
- Is: ultra-modular slide snippets, one-pager battlecard, and operational artifacts (canary script, SLO template, cost preview) intended to be copy-paste ready.
- Is not: a full enterprise procurement pack or legal contract. If they ask for that, escalate to AE and Solutions.

Core value messages (short snippets for slide headers):
- Predictable latency & cost — profiles per model variant
- Fast onramp for platform teams — VPC-friendly quickstart in <24h
- Safe default fallbacks — automatic model downgrades and cross-region routing
- Economic levers you control — batching, cache, quantization toggles

Modular slide snippets (copy-paste ready)
1) Opener: "Pilot in a Day — What we’ll prove"
   - 45m integration to demo endpoint
   - Canary steady-state at X qps with target p99 < 250ms (example)
   - Cost estimate: $Y/day for demo traffic (preview widget screenshot)

2) Techslide: "How we keep latency predictable"
   - Serving runtime selects kernels by model and sequence length
   - Prefix/KV caching and micro-batching for tail latency
   - Built-in fallbacks: model variants + cross-region routing

3) Security & Compliance: "Audit-friendly by design"
   - VPC/private control plane option + KMS hooks
   - Audit logs and per-team access control
   - Data residency/air-gapped packaging available on request

4) Pilot plan: "30/60/90 (pilot outcomes)"
   - 0–30d: integration + proof-of-concept, functional pass/fail criteria
   - 31–60d: load-driven canary + performance tuning (batching/quantization)
   - 61–90d: success criteria: SLA signatures, cost baseline, rollout plan

5) Economics snapshot: "Unit economics you can measure"
   - Key metrics: cost-per-1k tokens, median/99th latency, tokens-per-second per GPU
   - Quick knobs: reduce cost by 20–40% via caching + quantized model variant (typical)

6) Next steps slide: "Ship a pilot — checklist (one meeting)"
   - Get API key & sample dataset (10–20 examples)
   - Provide network allowlist, preferred region, and target QPS
   - Run quick canary with provided script (link to artifact)

One-pager battlecard (for rapid answer during objection):
- Common objection: "We can’t accept a managed service."
  - Rapid reply: "We offer Private (VPC) with customer-managed control plane; we can also ship an on-prem package for air-gapped flows."
- Common objection: "Latency will be unpredictable at scale."
  - Rapid reply: "We pilot with model variants and autoscaling policies; we include p99 tracing and token-level latency breakdowns so you see root cause in the first canary run."
- Common objection: "We need price predictability."
  - Rapid reply: "Reserved Dedicated capacity with burst options provides predictable throughput; we can simulate spend for your QPS in the pilot."

Canned scripts & artifacts (attach to pilot bundle)
- canary-run.sh (bash) — spins workload at target QPS, records p50/p95/p99, token counts
- slo-template.yaml — suggested SLOs and alert thresholds (api error rate, token latency, cost burn rate)
- procurement-onepager.pdf — one-page cost + SLA summary for finance & procurement

Quick operational play: "Skip the friction" (what SE does in the meeting)
- Minute 0–5: opener and ask for network allowlist and sample payloads
- Minute 5–10: drop the canary-run.sh link in chat and confirm region + QPS
- Minute 10–15: share the procurement-onepager and ask who in finance needs a 1-pager; offer to follow up with a tailored cost run
- Follow-up: create pilot folder in customer S3, share S3 path + credentials, schedule a 30m tuning session for week+1

Pilot success metrics (examples to propose)
- Functional: 95% of responses within acceptance criteria for downstream app
- Performance: p99 < target SLO (typical 200–300ms for short prompts)
- Economic: cost-per-1k tokens <= target derived from sample traffic

Fallbacks & escalation map (quick reference)
- If latency spike persists after tuning -> enable fallback model variant + route traffic to a different region; notify SRE and SE
- If cost burns > projected -> pause non-critical background traffic, enable tighter caching TTLs, revert to smaller model for non-critical endpoints
- If procurement stalls -> send procurement-onepager + contract-exception template to AE

Notes to self / open questions (work-in-progress):
- Should we include a pre-approved security questionnaire for midmarket? (Priya to check with security)
- Add a tiny interactive widget example showing cost delta when toggling quantization (Leo owns)
- Need better example numbers for p99 targets per model family (Maya to pull from benchmark sheet)

Suggested minimal pilot attachments (links to provide in meeting chat):
- canary-run.sh (hosted in GH gist)
- slo-template.yaml (paste as gist)
- procurement-onepager.pdf (one-page slide export)

Suggested next steps for this doc:
- Priya: confirm security-approved questionnaire existence (due 2024-11-20)
- Leo: prototype cost-delta widget (due 2024-12-05)
- Maya: extract example latency numbers from bench exports and fill slide snippet (due 2024-12-01)
- Evan: stitch assets into a single ZIP and make a meeting-friendly Google Drive folder (due 2024-12-08)

Scratch notes (for SEs to copy during calls):
- "We’ll get you a sandbox API key and a canary script in this meeting — at the end you’ll have objective numbers for p50/p99 and a cost preview."
- "If you need on-prem or VPC, we have a fast-track checklist and Ops will give an ETA."
- "Typical tuning paths: enable prefix cache, increase batch size up to X until latency hits target, then ramp QPS."

Version history:
- v0.1 (this file): initial assembly of snippets and checklist — rough numbers, WIP attachments

End of doc.
